class.name: DataSchema
class.brief_description: Describes the fields of a data file and validates data against them, for any format.

method.name: add_field
method.description: Adds [param field] at the end of [member fields].

method.name: convert_value
method.description: Converts [param text] (a CSV cell, an XML attribute) to the type of the field [param field_name]. Empty text gives [member DataField.default_value]. Returns [code]null[/code] if the text does not convert, and prints an error if the field does not exist.

method.name: create_from_dictionary
method.description: Creates a schema from a short form: each key is a field name, each value a [enum Variant.Type], a [Dictionary] (a [Dictionary] field with that nested schema) or an [Array] with one element (an [Array] field with that element type or element schema). The fields are [member DataField.required].

method.name: create_from_resource
method.description: Creates a schema from the stored properties of [param resource], the properties that [ResourceTextSerializer] writes. Pass an instance of a class or script to describe its layout (for example [code]MyItem.new()[/code]). Each property becomes an optional [DataField] with its type; enum and range hints are kept. A built-in resource property becomes a [Dictionary] field with a nested schema, a resource saved in a file is a [String] field (its path), and a resource property that is not set stays untyped because it can be either. An array gets the [member DataField.element_type] of its typed elements; an array of built-in resources, or an empty array of a script class, gets an [member DataField.element_schema]. The properties of [Resource] itself ([member Resource.resource_name], [member Resource.resource_local_to_scene]) are left out. With [member SerializerOptions.enums_as_names] (the default), enum properties are [String] fields with the names. Extra fields are allowed, so the type marker of the text formats passes. Cycles are cut at a depth of 6 levels. In the editor, the inspector of a [DataSchema] has the button [b]Generate from Resource...[/b] that does this for a chosen class.

method.name: find_field
method.description: Returns the index of the field [param name] in [member fields], or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: remove_field
method.description: Removes the field at [param index] from [member fields].

method.name: validate
method.description: Validates [param data] (a [Dictionary], an [Array] of [Dictionary] records or an [Array] of rows) and returns every issue with its field, path, row and column. Other data gives one [constant DataValidation.ISSUE_KIND_TYPE_MISMATCH]. [param options] limits the number of issues; [code]null[/code] keeps at most 1000. Each value is checked in this order: missing ([member DataField.required]), empty ([member DataField.allow_empty]), type ([member DataField.type]), range or enum ([member DataField.hint]), [member DataField.pattern], nested schemas; then [member DataField.unique] across rows. Keys that are not fields are handled by [member extra_fields]. [b]Note:[/b] [method validate] has no text, so issues get no lines. Use [method TextDataFormat.validate], or [method DataValidation.resolve_lines] with the text (for [JSON]).

members.member: With [constant EXTRA_FIELDS_MATCH_TEMPLATE], every key that is not in [member fields] is validated against this field. For example, a template of type [Dictionary] with a nested [member DataField.schema] validates every section of an [INI] file.
What happens with keys and columns that are not in [member fields].
The fields, in file order (the column order of a CSV file without header).

Glob patterns of the files this schema describes (such as [code]"res://data/items_*.csv"[/code]). Used by the editor to find the schema of an open file when this schema is listed in [member ProjectSettings.filesystem/data/schema_files]; not used at runtime, where the schema is passed to [method validate] directly.

constants.constant: Keys and columns that are not in [member fields] are reported as [constant DataValidation.ISSUE_KIND_UNKNOWN_FIELD]. Catches typos.
Keys and columns that are not in [member fields] are accepted without checks.
Keys and columns that are not in [member fields] are validated against [member extra_field_template].
Represents the size of the [enum ExtraFields] enum.
